questions.prompt: What is a team prompt playbook?

options.text: A shared set of tested prompts for the team's common tasks, each with an owner.
options.explanation: Right. It turns good individual prompts into the team's shared way of working.

options.text: A list of rules that bans staff from writing any prompts of their own at work.
options.explanation: A playbook covers common tasks. People can still prompt freely for one-off work.

options.text: A record of every chat each person on the team has had with the AI assistant.
options.explanation: A chat log is not a playbook. A playbook holds a few tested, reusable prompts.

questions.prompt: Why use a template with blanks, like [paste the email here], in a play?

options.text: Blanks make the model work faster and use fewer tokens on each request.
options.explanation: Blanks are for people, not speed. They show which part changes each time.

options.text: The tested parts stay the same, and people only fill in what changes.
options.explanation: Right. Everyone gets the same tested setup.

options.text: Models refuse any prompt that is not written in the form of a template.
options.explanation: Models accept any prompt. Templates are for consistency across the team.

questions.prompt: Your team moves to a new model version. What does OpenAI's guide say about your prompts?

options.text: Prompts behave the same on every model version, so no action is needed at all.
options.explanation: The guide says different snapshots can give different results.

options.text: Versions can give different results, so keep tests and re-run them when you upgrade.
options.explanation: Right. The guide suggests pinning a fixed version and keeping tests that show how prompts behave when you upgrade.

options.text: All prompts must be fully rewritten from scratch for each new model version.
options.explanation: The guide asks you to test, not to rewrite everything. Fix only what fails.
